chk_332e294219eb_0000.documentTitle: Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms
chk_332e294219eb_0000.sectionPath: Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms
chk_332e294219eb_0000.text:
Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms

> Synthetic demonstration reference for the dashboard's demo mode. It summarises general terms and names standards without quoting them.

chk_332e294219eb_0001.documentTitle: Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms
chk_332e294219eb_0001.sectionPath: Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms › Efficiency terms
chk_332e294219eb_0001.text:
Efficiency terms

Power usage effectiveness (PUE) is the total facility energy divided by the energy of the IT equipment; ISO/IEC 30134-2 defines it. ASHRAE 90.4 sets energy requirements for data centres.

chk_332e294219eb_0002.documentTitle: Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms
chk_332e294219eb_0002.sectionPath: Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms › Temperatures and differences
chk_332e294219eb_0002.text:
Temperatures and differences

Delta-T is the difference between the return and supply water temperatures. A low delta-T means more water is pumped for the same cooling load.

chk_332e294219eb_0003.documentTitle: Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms
chk_332e294219eb_0003.sectionPath: Demo reference card: data centre cooling terms › Redundancy
chk_332e294219eb_0003.text:
Redundancy

N+1 redundancy keeps one more chiller, pump or cooling tower available than the load needs, so one unit can be serviced, or can fail, without losing cooling.

chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0000.text:
Demo chiller maintenance guide

> Synthetic demonstration document written for this dashboard's demo mode. It is not a manufacturer manual, a standard or site documentation. On a real plant, follow the equipment manufacturer's instructions.

chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0001.sectionPath: Demo chiller maintenance guide › Performance indicators
chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0001.text:
Performance indicators

Chiller efficiency is tracked as the coefficient of performance (COP): the cooling delivered divided by the electrical power drawn. kW per ton expresses the same quantity the other way round, so a rising kW/ton means falling efficiency.

The condenser approach is the difference between the saturated condensing temperature and the leaving condenser water temperature. The evaporator approach is the difference between the leaving chilled water temperature and the saturated evaporating temperature. Both are logged once per shift and compared with the commissioning values.

chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0002.sectionPath: Demo chiller maintenance guide › Common causes of low COP
chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0002.text:
Common causes of low COP

Condenser tube fouling insulates the tubes, which raises the condenser approach and the head pressure, so the compressor needs more power for the same load and low COP results.

Non-condensable gases collect in the condenser and raise the condensing pressure; a high condenser approach with a clean tube bundle indicates them.

A low refrigerant charge lowers the evaporating pressure and causes a high evaporator approach and reduced efficiency.

High condenser water temperature from the cooling towers raises the refrigerant lift, so each ton of cooling costs more compressor power.

A low chilled-water delta-T at part load makes extra chillers run lightly loaded, which lowers the efficiency of the whole plant.

chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0003.sectionPath: Demo chiller maintenance guide › Condenser tube cleaning procedure
chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0003.text:
Condenser tube cleaning procedure

This procedure removes condenser tube fouling and scale deposits. Clean the tubes when the condenser approach has risen well above its commissioning value and non-condensable gases have been ruled out.

1. Stage the chiller off and confirm that another chiller has taken the load.
2. Stop the condenser water pump that feeds this chiller and close the condenser isolation valves.
3. Drain the water side of the condenser and open the water boxes.
4. Brush the tubes, flush them with clean water and inspect the tube sheet for scale deposits.
5. Close the water boxes, refill and vent the condenser, and return the chiller to service.
6. Record the condenser approach at a comparable load and compare it with the value before cleaning.

chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0004.sectionPath: Demo chiller maintenance guide › Refrigerant leak inspection
chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0004.text:
Refrigerant leak inspection

A refrigerant leak shows as a low refrigerant charge: low suction pressure, a high evaporator approach and, over time, reduced efficiency. Check flanged joints, valve packings and the run time of the purge unit, which rises when air enters a low-pressure machine.

Refrigerant handling follows the site's refrigerant safety rules and the applicable standard, for example EN 378 in Europe.

chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0005.sectionPath: Demo chiller maintenance guide › Compressor surge
chk_6479a9d1fdaf_0005.text:
Compressor surge

Compressor surge in a centrifugal chiller is a reversal of refrigerant flow at high lift and low load. It is heard as a loud noise and felt as vibration, and repeated surging damages the compressor. High condenser water temperature raises the lift and makes surge more likely. Condenser tube fouling has the same effect.

chk_6846dc086ef9_0000.text:
Demo cooling tower performance notes

> Synthetic demonstration notes for the dashboard's demo mode. They are not a manufacturer's data or a standard.

chk_6846dc086ef9_0001.sectionPath: Demo cooling tower performance notes › Approach and range
chk_6846dc086ef9_0001.text:
Approach and range

The tower approach is the difference between the cold water leaving the tower and the wet-bulb temperature of the entering air. The cooling range is the difference between the hot water entering the tower and the cold water leaving it. At a fixed load, a rising approach means the tower is rejecting heat less effectively.

chk_6846dc086ef9_0002.sectionPath: Demo cooling tower performance notes › Causes of poor tower performance
chk_6846dc086ef9_0002.text:
Causes of poor tower performance

Fill fouling and scale buildup reduce the wetted surface of the fill media, which raises the approach and causes high condenser water temperature.

A fan failure on one cell reduces the airflow, so the remaining cells cannot hold the condenser water setpoint on a hot day.

Low flow through a cell, for example from blocked spray nozzles, leaves dry patches in the fill and raises the leaving water temperature.

Biological growth fouls the fill and the basin and is a health risk, so water treatment and blowdown are kept under control.

chk_6846dc086ef9_0003.sectionPath: Demo cooling tower performance notes › Inspection checklist
chk_6846dc086ef9_0003.text:
Inspection checklist

1. Check each fan, gearbox and motor for vibration and abnormal noise.
2. Inspect the drift eliminator for damage; damaged eliminators increase drift loss.
3. Check the spray nozzles and the fill media for fouling and scale deposits.
4. Confirm the basin level and the make-up valve; a low basin level can starve the condenser water pumps.

chk_6846dc086ef9_0004.sectionPath: Demo cooling tower performance notes › Plant notes
chk_6846dc086ef9_0004.text:
Plant notes

Cooling tower 1 to Cooling tower 4 share a common condenser water header. Cooling tower 4 serves the header only when its fan is available. Where a contract requires a thermal performance acceptance test, it follows CTI ATC-105.

chk_751ada316473_0000.text:
Demo pump troubleshooting guide

> Synthetic demonstration guide for the dashboard's demo mode, covering the condenser water and chilled water pumps. It is not a manufacturer manual.

chk_751ada316473_0001.text:
Cavitation

Cavitation is the formation and collapse of vapour bubbles at the impeller when the pressure at the pump suction falls too low. It sounds like gravel passing through the pump. Cavitation causes vibration and, over time, erodes the impeller. A clogged strainer on the suction side is a common cause, because it adds pressure drop before the pump.

chk_751ada316473_0002.sectionPath: Demo pump troubleshooting guide › Bearing wear
chk_751ada316473_0002.text:
Bearing wear

Bearing wear shows as rising vibration and a higher bearing temperature. Shaft misalignment between the motor and the pump increases the bearing load and leads to bearing wear, so check the coupling alignment after any motor work.

chk_751ada316473_0003.sectionPath: Demo pump troubleshooting guide › Seal leaks
chk_751ada316473_0003.text:
Seal leaks

A mechanical seal leak shows as water at the seal gland. Running the pump dry, or with abrasive water, causes seal failure.

chk_751ada316473_0004.sectionPath: Demo pump troubleshooting guide › Standby pump rotation procedure
chk_751ada316473_0004.text:
Standby pump rotation procedure

This procedure prevents bearing wear and stuck valves on standby pumps that stand idle for weeks.

1. Run CW pump 4, the standby condenser water pump, for one hour each week and log its vibration and motor current.
2. Run CHW pump 4, the standby chilled water pump, on the same day.
3. Exercise the isolation valve of each standby pump during the run.

chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0000.documentTitle: Demo site note: chilled water plant sequence
chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0000.sectionPath: DEMO SITE NOTE: CHILLED WATER PLANT SEQUENCE
chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0000.text:
DEMO SITE NOTE: CHILLED WATER PLANT SEQUENCE

Synthetic demonstration note for the dashboard's demo plant. It is not a real site's sequence of operation.

chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0001.documentTitle: Demo site note: chilled water plant sequence
chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0001.sectionPath: DEMO SITE NOTE: CHILLED WATER PLANT SEQUENCE › 1.1 Normal operation
chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0001.text:
1.1 Normal operation
Chiller 1 and Chiller 2 run in normal operation, and Chiller 3 is the lag chiller. CHW pump 1 serves Chiller 1, CHW pump 2 serves Chiller 2 and CHW pump 3 serves Chiller 3. The chilled water supply temperature setpoint is 7 °C.

chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0002.documentTitle: Demo site note: chilled water plant sequence
chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0002.sectionPath: DEMO SITE NOTE: CHILLED WATER PLANT SEQUENCE › 1.2 Staging
chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0002.text:
1.2 Staging
The lag chiller starts when the running chillers are fully loaded or when the chilled water supply rises above its setpoint. A low chilled water delta-T makes the plant start chillers early, so check the control valves of the CRAH units in the data hall before adding a chiller.

chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0003.documentTitle: Demo site note: chilled water plant sequence
chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0003.sectionPath: DEMO SITE NOTE: CHILLED WATER PLANT SEQUENCE › 1.3 Free cooling
chk_98c1a7b7adaf_0003.text:
1.3 Free cooling
When the wet-bulb temperature is low enough, the plate heat exchanger provides free cooling and the chillers stage off.

chk_d21cc6c815f8_0000.documentTitle: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0000.sectionPath: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0000.text:
Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning

This procedure removes condenser tube fouling on Chiller 2.

> Synthetic demonstration procedure for the dashboard's demo plant (3 chillers, 4 cooling towers, 4 condenser water and 4 chilled water pumps). It is not a real site's procedure.

chk_d21cc6c815f8_0001.documentTitle: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0001.sectionPath: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning › Scope
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0001.text:
Scope

CW pump 2 feeds Chiller 2, and the condenser water from Chiller 2 returns to the cooling towers through the common header. Chiller 1 and Chiller 3 carry the load while Chiller 2 is out of service.

chk_d21cc6c815f8_0002.documentTitle: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0002.sectionPath: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning › Isolation steps
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0002.text:
Isolation steps

1. Confirm that Chiller 1 and Chiller 3 can carry the cooling load at the current wet-bulb temperature.
2. Stage Chiller 2 off from the plant controls and wait for its compressor to stop.
3. Stop CW pump 2, then close the condenser isolation valves of Chiller 2.
4. Close the chilled water isolation valves of Chiller 2 and stop CHW pump 2 if no other chiller needs it.
5. Lock out the motor of CW pump 2 before the water boxes are opened.

chk_d21cc6c815f8_0003.documentTitle: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0003.sectionPath: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning › Cleaning and inspection
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0003.text:
Cleaning and inspection

Brush and flush the condenser tubes. Note any scale deposits or tube damage, because scale buildup returns quickly when water treatment is poor.

chk_d21cc6c815f8_0004.documentTitle: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0004.sectionPath: Demo site procedure: Chiller 2 condenser tube cleaning › Return to service
chk_d21cc6c815f8_0004.text:
Return to service

Refill and vent the condenser and open its isolation valves. Start CW pump 2 and confirm the flow at the flow meter before staging Chiller 2 back on. Record the condenser approach at a comparable load; a clean condenser shows an approach close to its commissioning value.
